newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FOCUS - Russian share bull pauses for breath.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Russian share bull pauses for breath.

text.p: Russian shares are taking a breather after stampeding higher recently, but investors' interest remains high and spectacular gains could spread to less well known stocks, traders and analysts said on Wednesday.

The Russian equities market, which set a record high on the Russian Trading System index on Friday, retreated this week and showed some of the volatility that charachterised it before its 40 percent rise in the first three weeks of January.

The 24-share index firmed to 275.50 at 1300 GMT on Wednesday from Tuesday's close of 268.37, but was still down from the record 293.33 set at Friday's close with operators confused about where the market was headed in the short term.
"I don't know where the rally came from," said one experienced Western trader early on Wednesday in response to a short-lived price rise in the absence of Western buying.
Domestic brokers who are often accused of using tight market liquidity to quickly mark up prices when demand appears, have been anticipating a new onslaught of Western orders.

But Western investors who drive this emerging market, which has seen market capitalisation jump from to $54 billion this week from $37 billion at the beginning of the month, Salomon Brothers said, are pausing before opening their wallets wider.
"Some shares have become dangerously close to being overbought, or even overpriced," said Gavin Rankin, director of research at Troika-Dialog in Moscow.
"The market overheats fairly rapidly, and demand for shares at times seems to be going beyond fundamental short-term value. Stocks need to pause for reflection at times."
James Fenkner, director of research at CentreInvest Securities, said Russian shares were still undervalued.
He said the price-earnings ratio for Russia was nine, based on Russian accounting standards and weighted by market capitalisation, less than half the S&P index in the U.S.
Russian growth potential also made the market a good buy, he said. "The whole telecoms industry had a 100 percent increase in revenue from the first half of 1995 to the first half of 1996.
"What we're looking at is a technical lull. People are looking for a good price," he said. "The market should firm in the middle of next week based purely on the technicals."

Equities analysts generally expect new funds to seek out less well known shares, though new money from mutual funds limited to investing in the top shares will continue to feed money into leading shares.
"Top shares have room to go, but they certainly don't have as much room to grow as the second tier," said Christopher Smart, director of research at Pioneer Securities.
Pavel Gronbjerg, co-head of equities trading at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in Moscow, said that finding cheap stocks was the key to the Russian market.
"Russia is not a growth story," he said. "It is an undervaluation story." --Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
